name: Waluj CETP (10 MLD)
effluent_source: Design capacity of the Waluj CETP, 10 MLD (CPCB, Assessment of the Need for CETPs, 2015); not a measured discharge
coord_status: aggregate — plotted at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar town centroid; individual CETP location not published
source_name: CPCB, Assessment of the Need for Common Effluent Treatment Plants (2015); Waluj CETP project presentation; Aurangabad CEPI Action Plan (MPCB)
notes: CETP for the Waluj MIDC industrial area; capacity 10 MLD with 20% overloading allowed; project started 2007, commissioned June 2011, project cost Rs 17 crore; extended-aeration activated sludge process; final discharge to the Kham River via underground pipeline (disposal line completed; CETP in operation from July 2011 per the Aurangabad CEPI action plan). name: Andhra Paper Limited, Rajahmundry
effluent_source: Sum of the two consented outlets in APPCB Consent to Operate renewal 03/07/2023: 21,169 KLD process & washings effluent after ETP treatment + 10,365 KLD cooling blowdown & boiler/DM plant regeneration = 31,534 KLD max daily discharge; not a measured discharge
coord_status: town-centroid — plotted at the Rajahmundry town centroid; no plant-site coordinates published
source_name: APPCB Consent to Operate renewal No. APPCB/VSP/RJY/361/CTO/HO/2010 dated 03/07/2023 (via NGT OA 33 of 2023 compliance record)
source_url: https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/sites/default/files/news_updates/OA 33 of 2023 Consolidated Compliance report filed by R7.pdf
notes: Integrated wood-based pulp and paper mill (commissioned 1964 as Andhra Pradesh Paper Mills; now Andhra Paper Ltd, West Coast Paper Mills group), 198.09 acres at Sriramnagar, Rajamahendravaram, on the west bank of the Godavari; EC for expansion to 500 TPD pulp / 330 TPD paper (2005). Treated process effluent goes to greenbelt development and the excess to the Turupu Lanka sand shoals in the middle of the Godavari through two Hume pipes, then an elaborate land-treatment system over 612 acres; cooling blowdown also to the sand shoals. 31.53 MLD is the maximum consented daily discharge, not the amount actually reaching the river (part is reused for greenbelt). Consent valid to 30/06/2028. NGT OA 33 of 2023 (SZ) is seized of complaints of air and water pollution from the mill (CPCB inspected; APPCB report pending as of Dec 2023); in May 2026 the AP Deputy CM (Environment) ordered an audit of pollutants entering the Godavari and specifically sought details on this mill's discharge. Official town name is Rajamahendravaram. Consented/design capacity figure, never a measured discharge, and is not added to any drain load.

name: Nashik Ambad–Satpur MIDC industrial belt
industry_type: Mixed industrial belt (engineering, auto components, pharma, food processing, distillery)
coord_status: aggregate — plotted at the Nashik town centroid; individual unit locations not published
source_name: CPCB, Assessment of the Need for CETPs (2015); Bombay High Court contempt proceedings on Godavari pollution, Oct–Nov 2026; Maharashtra Chief Secretary review meeting, 04/11/2026
notes: No CETP exists in the Ambad or Satpur MIDC estates: CPCB's 2015 assessment lists a 0.500 MLD CETP as 'needed/proposed' for each estate, and as of Nov 2026 the CETP is still not built — the Bombay High Court (contempt petition, Oct 2026) and the Chief Secretary's review (04/11/2026) record that MIDC was given time to obtain instructions on installing it, and the project 'gathered momentum only after the contempt petition was filed'. MPCB sampling on 05/10/2026 found chromium contamination in the Nandini tributary (not the main channel) and, at the Godavari–Kapila confluence, Tapovan: BOD 85 mg/l, DO nil, COD 196 mg/l. The Chief Secretary directed MPCB to inspect/raid suspected units, fix responsibility on officials who allowed violations despite Zero Liquid Discharge consent conditions, and prepare a list of the most polluting industries with owners' details. MPCB's 2018 region-wise table counts 67 highly polluting industries in the Nashik region (22 distilleries, 35 sugar, 4 fertilizer, 2 pharma, 1 pesticide, 3 thermal power) — a region total, not a Godavari-basin count. No published aggregate effluent figure for the belt exists, so effluent is blank. No effluent figure is attributed to this cluster.

name: Nanded MIDC industrial estate (Vasarni CETP)
industry_type: Mixed industrial estate (agro-based: edible oil, dairy, drugs)
coord_status: aggregate — plotted at the Nanded town centroid; individual unit locations not published
source_name: MPCB affidavit in Bombay High Court PIL 17/2011 (15/12/2011); MPCB affidavit in NGT OA 92/2025 (WZ), 02/09/2025
notes: A CETP at Vasarni, Nanded is listed among the CETPs monitored by MPCB in the Board's 15/12/2011 affidavit to the Bombay High Court, but no capacity, member count or discharge figure for it is published anywhere found, so effluent is blank. MIDC Nanded has 320 industries (33 red, 95 orange, 192 green); only 10 operate and generate effluent, mostly agro-based edible-oil extraction/refining units that are seasonal, plus Godavari Drugs Ltd; the Government Milk Scheme unit stands 800 m from the Godavari at Vasarni, all other effluent-generating units more than 1.5 km away. A 1998–2000 study (Deshmukh & Ambore, J. Industrial Pollution Control) found untreated MIDC effluent reaching the Godavari by nala with heavy metals above limits; no recent published effluent figure exists. The NGT OA 92/2025 affidavit (02/09/2025) records Nanded city sewage (70 MLD generated, 67 MLD treated) but no industrial effluent figure. No effluent figure is attributed to this cluster.

name: Ramagundam industrial belt (NTPC, RFCL, Singareni, cement)
industry_type: Thermal power, coal mining, fertilizer and cement belt
drain_name: Godavari (catchment only — no direct discharge consented)
coord_status: aggregate — plotted at the Ramagundam town centroid; individual plant locations not published
source_name: NTPC Ramagundam six-monthly EC compliance report, Oct 2023–Mar 2024; NGT Southern Zone order on NTPC Ramagundam 2x800 MW EC
notes: Belt comprises NTPC Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station (2,600 MW), Ramagundam Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd (RFCL, urea), Singareni Collieries mines (Godavarikhani), Kesoram/UltraTech cement and TSGENCO Ramagundam-B. No CETP exists in the belt and no published aggregate industrial discharge figure exists, so effluent is blank. NTPC's environmental clearance stipulates 'there shall be no direct discharge into the river Godavari'; ash-pond water is treated in the ash-water recirculation system (AWRS) and reused, with augmentation under way for complete reuse (HYC report, Mar 2024). The NGT Southern Zone, hearing the challenge to the 2x800 MW expansion EC, noted the project claimed Zero Liquid Discharge but was permitted to discharge treated water into the Godavari during monsoon. Press and activist accounts (Nov 2026 NGT petition) allege untreated effluent from NTPC, Jaipur Thermal Plant, RFCL and Basantnagar Cement reaches the river; these are allegations, not published measurements. No effluent figure is attributed to this cluster.

name: ITC Paperboards & Specialty Papers Division, Bhadrachalam
coord_status: town-centroid — plotted at the Bhadrachalam town centroid; no plant-site coordinates published
source_name: ITC Ltd PSPD Bhadrachalam — CII-GBC National Award case study (2008); WaterWorld ultrafiltration case study (2007)
notes: India's largest paperboard plant (about 300,000 TPA at the time of the case studies), on the Godavari at Bhadrachalam (mill at Sarapaka), with its own effluent treatment plant; elemental chlorine-free pulp mill; ISO-14001 certified. The CII case study records a 50% reduction in freshwater consumption and a 25% reduction in wastewater discharge from water-conservation measures, but no absolute effluent volume or consented discharge to the river is published, so effluent is blank. Bhadrachalam is on CPCB's polluted Godavari stretch (Basara–Mancherial–Ramagundam–Kaleshwaram–Bhadrachalam, BOD max 24 mg/l, Priority II, CPCB 2022), but the stretch BOD is not attributable to the mill. No effluent figure is attributed to this plant.

name: Mancherial–Bellampalli coal belt (Singareni mines, STPP)
industry_type: Coal mining and thermal power belt
coord_status: aggregate — plotted at the Mancherial town centroid; individual mine/plant locations not published
source_name: TSPCB Consent to Operate renewal, GDK 2&2A incline mine, SCCL, Godavarikhani, 14/03/2017; Singareni Thermal Power Plant (Wikipedia)
notes: Coal belt of the Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL): Bellampalli/Mancherial has the state's densest concentration of coal mines (SCCL operates 18 opencast and 29 underground mines across six Telangana districts including Mancherial), plus the Singareni Thermal Power Plant (2x600 MW) at Jaipur, Mancherial district. No CETP exists in the belt and no published aggregate mine-water or industrial discharge figure exists, so effluent is blank. As an example of the scale of individual consents, TSPCB's 14/03/2017 consent for SCCL's GDK 2&2A incline mine at Godavarikhani allows excess mine discharge of 1,560 KLD (1.56 MLD) to a nearby drain after treatment in a settling tank and sand filter beds — one mine only, not summed here. Town sewage from Mancherial/Mandamarri reaches the Godavari via the Rallavagu and Thollavagu streams (NGT petition, Nov 2026). No effluent figure is attributed to this cluster.

name: Kothagudem Thermal Power Station, Paloncha
drain_name: Karakavagu → Kinnerasani River (tributary of the Godavari)
coord_status: town-centroid — plotted at the Kothagudem town centroid; the plant is at Paloncha, about 10 km from Kothagudem town; no plant-site coordinates published
source_name: Telangana High Court order in PIL 224/2014 (Balineni Satyanarayana vs Govt of Telangana), 17/02/2022, reproducing the TSPCB inspection report
notes: Kothagudem Thermal Power Station (KTPS, TSGENCO) at Paloncha, stages V (500 MW), VI (500 MW) and VII (800 MW); older units phased out 2019–Mar 2020. Per the TSPCB report reproduced in the High Court order, all three operating stages have effluent treatment systems; all effluents including ash washings go to the ETPs and treated effluent is discharged into the Karakavagu, which joins the Kinnerasani River (a Godavari tributary; the Kinnerasani stretch at Khammam is CPCB Priority V, BOD max 6 mg/l). Decanted ash-pond water from stages V & VI is partly supplied to farmers for irrigation and the remainder discharged into the Karakavagu; stage VII decanted ash-pond water discharges into the Kinnerasani. TSPCB samples of 07/07/2021 were within Board standards for surface water. No discharge flow figure is published, so effluent is blank. NGT imposed a Rs 4 crore penalty on KTPS for not achieving 100% ash utilisation (per a 2024 writ petition). No effluent figure is attributed to this plant.

name: Chandrapur–Ballarpur industrial belt (Wardha)
industry_type: Pulp and paper, thermal power and cement belt
coord_status: aggregate — plotted at the Ballarpur town centroid; individual plant locations not published
source_name: MPCB, Report on Action Plan for Clean-up of Polluted Stretch of Purna River (June 2019), Table 16 — Highly Polluting Industries as on 31/03/2018; CPCB Polluted River Stretches 2022 (Wardha)
notes: Belt on the Wardha River (which joins the Wainganga to form the Pranhita, a Godavari tributary): BILT Ballarpur paper mill (Ballarpur Industries Ltd, writing & printing paper), Chandrapur Super Thermal Power Station, and cement plants (UltraTech/ACC) drawing Wardha water. MPCB's region-wise table (as on 31/03/2018) counts 18 highly polluting industries in the Chandrapur region — 5 cement, 2 dyes & dye-intermediates, 1 integrated iron & steel, 1 pulp & paper, 2 sugar, 7 thermal power — a region total, not a Wardha-basin count. No CETP exists in the belt. No consented river-discharge figure for the Ballarpur mill was found: a 2012 MPCB consent retrieved is for BILT's Ashti unit (Gadchiroli), not Ballarpur, so it is not used. BILT has been in corporate insolvency since 2019 (NCLT Mumbai; resolution plan approved Mar 2023), so the mill's current operating status is uncertain. The Wardha stretch along Chandrapur–Ballarpur is CPCB Priority II (BOD max not stated in the 2022 summary table excerpt). No effluent figure is attributed to this cluster.
